facts.statement: Tytthostonyx was a genus of prehistoric seabird.
facts.quote: Tytthostonyx is a genus of prehistoric seabird.

facts.statement: The only known species of this genus is Tytthostonyx glauconiticus.
facts.quote: A single species is placed herein, Tytthostonyx glauconiticus.

facts.statement: Tytthostonyx was placed in its own family, Tytthostonychidae.
facts.quote: It has been placed into a family of its own, Tytthostonychidae.

facts.statement: Tytthostonyx fossils were found in the Hornerstown Formation at the Cretaceous–Paleogene boundary, approximately 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Found in the much-debated Hornerstown Formation which straddles the Cretaceous–Paleogene boundary 66 million years ago

facts.statement: The time range for Tytthostonyx is from the Maastrichtian to the Danian, spanning 72.2 to 61.66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Maastrichtian to Danian (72.2 to 61.66 million years ago)

facts.statement: Tytthostonyx was apparently closely related to the ancestors of modern seabirds like Procellariiformes and/or Pelecaniformes.
facts.quote: this animal was apparently closely related to the ancestor of some modern birds, such as Procellariiformes and/or "Pelecaniformes".

facts.statement: The genus Tytthostonyx was described by Olson and Parris in 1987.
The Hornerstown Formation, where Tytthostonyx fossils were found, is the subject of much debate.
facts.quote: Found in the much-debated Hornerstown Formation

rejected.statement: Tytthostonyx belongs to the class Aves.
